title: Peregrin and the Gentle Ogre
markdown:
Peregrin the young wizard lived on the dark pine-covered slopes of Owlglass Mountain. His cottage smelled of rosemary and, sometimes, the sweet slightly burnt sugar that magic left behind. Sunlight, when it peeked through dense pine, painted light and dark on the worn wooden floor. His best friend, most of the time his only companion, was Scruffy: a lizard whose scales shimmered like lots of tiny emeralds. A rather sleepy pet, with a talent for finding the warmest spots—Peregrin’s shoulder, or on chilly days the pocket of his robe.

One crisp morning the market bell chimed in the distance, a sound that usually made Peregrin’s heart flip. Today it made him frown. He had promised Mrs. Higgins the rare Moonpetal bloom for her special honey cakes. Moonpetals bloomed only under soft moonlight, petals with a shine like starlight. Yesterday, in haste, he had accidentally traded the last precious Moonpetal for a rather nice, slightly wobbly walking stick that looked so much like a badger. He had been charmed by its twitching wooden nose. Mrs. Higgins was expecting the flower. The market would buzz soon. He needed to fix this before the first stall opened its shutters.

“Come on, Scruffy. We need to find another Moonpetal. And try to stay awake this time. I have a feeling we might need your keen eyes. Or at least, not your napping abilities.”

Scruffy blinked golden eyes the colour of warm honey and flicked his tail. He scuttled onto Peregrin’s shoulder, settling by the ear, and let out a tiny contented sigh like a small gust of wind.

They ventured into the whispering pine woods climbing Owlglass. Cool air, fresh pine, damp earthy forest floor. Sunlight dappled the mossy ground. Peregrin hummed a jaunty tune about brave knights and mischievous sprites as he searched for a silvery glow. Under velvety ferns. Behind old tree roots that twisted like fingers.

“Here, Scruffy. Do you see it? The Moonpetal should be right… oh.”

Scruffy, perched on Peregrin’s outstretched finger, tiny claws tickling, was now fast asleep. Emerald body curled, head on tail. Tiny snores like leaves skittering.

“Oh, Scruffy.” A fond smile. He scooped the sleeping lizard into his cloak pocket, snug. “Just me then. Two eyes, and a slightly worried feeling in my tummy.”

He walked deeper, trees closer, branches weaving a protective ceiling, shadows dancing. Then a soft muffled sound, like a giant sigh caught in a thick cloud. Full of sadness.

Through hanging ivy: a truly huge creature sitting with knees pulled to his chest. An ogre, very big, and by the looks of him very gloomy. Not roaring or stomping. Sad. Big gentle eyes the colour of deep pools, watching a ladybug meticulously crawl up a blade of grass.

“Hello?” A little shaky, trying to sound brave.

The ogre jumped like a small landslide of pebbles and hid his face behind massive tree-trunk hands. “Please don’t be cross. I didn’t mean to be so big. It just happens.”

Peregrin was not scared. The voice was so gentle, the eyes so worried. “I’m not cross. I’m Peregrin. Are you alright? You look rather thoughtful.”

The ogre peeked through enormous fingers. “I’m Grumbles. Everyone runs away. They think I’m going to stomp or roar or eat their hats. But I just like watching ladybugs.” He pointed a huge thick finger, calloused like old bark. “She’s very determined. I admire her spirit.”

Peregrin chuckled, light and clear. “She certainly is. I’m looking for a Moonpetal. Have you seen any?”

A flicker of hope. “They grow near my favourite quiet spot, by the gurgling brook. I always leave them be. Too pretty to pick. Little fallen stars.” He stood slowly; the ground shook just a little. “I can show you. If you’re not afraid of me.”

“Not at all.” Peregrin pulled Scruffy from his pocket. The lizard blinked sleepily, stretching emerald limbs. “Scruffy, meet Grumbles. He’s not very talkative before his second nap, which is usually around elevenses.”

Grumbles’s rugged face cracked into a shy smile, few but rather large teeth. “A very small creature. Like a jewel. A very sleepy jewel.”

Together they walked toward the brook. Grumbles moved with surprising grace, enormous feet treading with remarkable care, like a dancer trying not to crush invisible flowers. Over roots, around bushes. Large hands occasionally steadying against a trunk, leaving no mark. He pointed, fingers stained from painting pebbles. “Just beyond those mossy rocks.”

A small patch of Moonpetals, silvery petals unfurling in dappled light, shimmering like captured moonlight. Peregrin gasped.

“Thank you, Grumbles.” He picked one carefully, stem cool and slender. “Mrs. Higgins will be so pleased. And I shall have to thank you properly. Not just for the flower. For being you.”

“It’s nice to help someone who isn’t afraid of me. A rather rare and pleasant experience.”

Peregrin looked at him truly. Not scary. Lonely. Size a barrier, shyness making it worse. “The market is opening soon. If you come with me, perhaps people will see how kind you are. And maybe you could have a stall selling your painted stones. I’ve seen them by the roadside. Each one a tiny colourful world.”

Grumbles looked at his large hands as if seeing them for the first time. Hesitant hope. “They wouldn’t run away screaming? Or throw rotten apples?”

“Not if you’re with me.” Peregrin placed Scruffy back on his shoulder. Scruffy, now fully awake, seemed to nod, little head bobbing.

At the bustling market Peregrin walked with confident purpose beside Grumbles, Moonpetal for Mrs. Higgins. He introduced the gentle ogre to everyone, explaining how he had helped find the rare flower. Folk accustomed to Peregrin’s friendly ways began to relax. They saw shy smiles, careful movements, then the stunning painted stones: miniature masterpieces of swirling colours. By the final market chime Grumbles had made several sales and, more importantly, several new friends. Peregrin felt a warmth better than a bubbling cauldron. Scruffy, nestled on his shoulder, let out a soft contented sigh, his third nap of the day quite happily avoided.
characters: Peregrin (young wizard who trades by accident), Scruffy (a lizard who finds the warmest spots)
